notDelivered.reason: NOT SUPPORTED, by client decision on 2026-08-22. Kwapso kit ruling 10 already put RTL out of scope; the commission asked for rtl:true and the client has now settled it as LTR-only.
notDelivered.note: The 65 primitives are nevertheless written with CSS logical properties throughout, and motion.css carries [dir=rtl] mirrors for the sheet, tab indicator and stepper connector. That was not reverted: reverting 65 files to physical properties would be pure risk for zero gain, and logical properties resolve identically in LTR. If RTL is ever wanted, the components are most of the way there and the missing piece is a Radix DirectionProvider at the app root.

The React API, the six sizes and the currentColor wiring were final throughout and none of them moved through either art swap; the NAMES were final only until the second swap below overturned that (docs/RULES.md §9.1 records the override).
notDelivered.resolution: DELIVERED 2026-08-27 as the Iconoir pack (MIT, 1,383 glyphs, stroke on a 24 grid), vendored over the placeholders under a fixed 93 + 3 commission contract bridged onto Iconoir's own names by an alias table. REPLACED WHOLESALE 2026-09-03: client ruling, verbatim, "the only icons that we are using are these icons from Phosphor... any previous icon that's on the repo or wherever, kill it" — the entire Iconoir pack was deleted, the alias table deleted, and the fixed-contract validation in generate-icons.mjs deleted with it. The kit now vendors Phosphor (MIT) whole — 1,512 glyphs, fill weight throughout except Plus/Power/Prohibit at regular weight — under Phosphor's own names with no translation layer. See iconArt.
notDelivered.swapProcedure: Drop the real <Name>.svg over the existing file (or a new name) in foundations/icons/, run `node foundations/icons/generate-icons.mjs`. No component and no call site changes for an existing name; a new name is simply a new export. The generator reads each file's own viewBox, so incoming art may be drawn on any grid, and validates only that the name is a legal JS identifier, the viewBox is present, and no colour is hardcoded — there is no fixed required-names list to update.

notDelivered.reason: --warning and --warning-foreground were SETTLED 2026-09-02: the client released two brand colours and --warning takes the orange #F7953E, with --warning-foreground at --ink-on-accent (charcoal, 7.79:1). --warning-strong is the ink half -- the warning WORD -- and did not move. Orange as text measures 2.23 on off-beige and 2.02 on soft paper, so it cannot take the fill; and nothing in components/ or compositions/ reads this token, so minting it a darkened orange (as ruling 43 gave poppy --kw-poppy-ink) would invent a hex for a consumer that does not exist. It resolves to --ink-primary.
notDelivered.recommendation: Leave at --ink-primary. Open a client ruling the day a component writes a warning in words.

notDelivered.item: A non-editorial quote register on ArticleBody
notDelivered.reason: ArticleBody draws every `blockquote` as ruling 13's pull-quote — SerrifCondensed at the h3 step on --tracking-serif, 24px, `my-[var(--space-8)]`, "one per page" by editorial rule — and there is no second register and no way to opt out: the treatment is unconditional descendant CSS on the root, and ArticleBodyProps carries no variant for it. The kit's law-book does not rule on quotes at all: `blockquote` appears in none of docs/RULES.md, PATTERN.md, BUILD-A-COMPONENT.md, BUILD-A-SCREEN.md or TOKENS.md, and the only other component that draws one (typography's `Headline as="blockquote"`) is documented as the same pull-quote. THE CASE THAT HAS NO ANSWER: a quoted reply inside a ticket or a meeting note — several per page, none of them editorial. `notes.tsx` names "a quoted reply" as a fully-composed row a call site supplies, which is the kit's model for a THREAD; it does not cover a quote a person typed mid-prose inside one body, which is what a consuming app receives when its editor emits HTML.
notDelivered.recommendation: A second register on ArticleBody, selected by a prop, for a quote that is a QUOTED PASSAGE rather than an editorial pull-quote — sans, body step, quiet ink, marked by a rule rather than by the serif — with the editorial rule kept as the default so nothing that draws a pull-quote today changes. Which of the two is the default, and what the non-editorial one looks like, is a design decision and is why this is logged rather than guessed (BUILD-A-COMPONENT: "A logged gap is fine. A guess that looks like law is not."). The kwapso app is holding a one-line app-side override against this entry and deletes it the day the register ships.

notDelivered.item: A chip row that mixes the toolbar pill's type step with CH11's
notDelivered.reason: The client's ruling of 2026-09-02 — "the filter button-pill it's still differnet than the other 2. fix and uniform it" — was applied to `CHIP_ADD` alone, which is the "+ filter" slot the toolbar draws beside `SortControl` and `ViewSwitch`. It is now 14/500 on 18 of inline padding, matching `selectTriggerVariants`. `filterChipVariants` — a REMOVABLE facet chip, and the "Clear filters" control that shares its drawing — was NOT moved: those are CH11's `.kw-chip`, drawn at badge type (12) on `px-3` in the fragment `filter-bar.tsx` cites, and the ruling names one pill against "the other 2", which is the add slot against sort and view. A chip is not one of the other 2, and re-deciding CH11 needs its own ruling rather than a designer's inference from a ruling about something else. Measured on verify/toolbar-writeback, light and dark: add slot 13.125px/500 at 16.875px inline padding, chip and Clear 11.25px/400 at 11.25px (a 15px root; 14/500/18 and 12/400/12 at 16).
notDelivered.recommendation: Ask the client whether a bar drawing BOTH chips and the add slot should carry two type steps in one row. The consuming app does not hit it today — its own ruling of the same day is that active filters are reported as a count inside the pill and never as chips, so its row holds exactly one pill — which is why this is logged rather than guessed at. If the answer is one step, the move is `filterChipVariants` and the Clear control to `text-sm`/`--space-4h`, and CH11's badge chip survives only where a chip sits inside a facet's results.

notDelivered.reason: `CompactFacet` (added 2026-09-02) holds ONE value or none, and `SearchableFacet` stays the multi-select drawing. A compact facet shows its value IN ITS TRIGGER, and a trigger holding a set has to summarise it — "3 selected", or a truncated run of names. Neither wording exists in the kit, and CH11's own answer to "several values are on" is the chip row `FilterBar` already draws. Inventing a summary string here would bake an untranslatable sentence into a component and would look like law.
notDelivered.recommendation: Open a client ruling on what a compact facet says when several options are on, then either add a `multiple` mode to `CompactFacet` or state that the multi-select case is `SearchableFacet` plus the chip row. Both consuming surfaces are single-value today (one value per query parameter), so nothing is blocked.

notDelivered.item: Arrow-key navigation inside a facet's option list
notDelivered.reason: Both `SearchableFacet` and `CompactFacet` draw their options as a `role="listbox"` of real `<button>`s, which is reachable and operable by Tab and Enter and is rung by tokens.css section 8 at each row's own radius — but it does not implement the roving-tabindex arrow-key pattern a native listbox has. `SearchableFacet` has shipped this way since it landed; `CompactFacet` matches it deliberately rather than introducing a second keyboard model for the same list. Radix's `Select` has the pattern, and is not usable here: its typeahead consumes the keystrokes a search field inside the panel needs, which is the whole reason a compact facet could not simply be a `Select` (the gap this version closed).
notDelivered.recommendation: One roving-tabindex helper for the facet list, applied to both facets in the same pass so they cannot diverge. Not attempted here: it is a behaviour change to a shipped component and belongs in its own change with its own verification, not folded into a write-back.

foundationsFolder.status: DONE — client ruled D10-B on 2026-08-24 after seeing the full cost drawn; tokens/, icons/ and motion/ now live under foundations/.
foundationsFolder.reason: The agreed structure groups tokens/, icons/ and motion/ under a foundations/ folder, and the folder is now made. The count in the superseded note was low: eighty tracked files reach the three folders by relative path, not thirteen — 14 decision and index pages under verify/, 11 verify harnesses (10 Tailwind entry sheets and one .tsx), 42 kit source files, 7 demo and mini-app files, and 6 documentation files, plus package.json, tsconfig.json, vite.config.ts, README.md and this manifest naming them without a '../'. Two further references pointed OUT of the moved folders and were missed by that grep entirely: foundations/tokens/tokens.css reached ../assets/fonts/ for its three @font-face rules, and foundations/icons/icon-base.tsx reached ../lib/utils. All were repaired. Every one of the fourteen decision pages was reopened in a browser afterwards and asserted styled — stylesheet count, computed body font-family and computed background — because a missing stylesheet is not an error in HTML and checking that the file exists is not checking that the page has its paper.
foundationsFolder.consumingApps: There is no exports map and no path alias — the kit is vendored source, so every import is a literal path. An app's two stylesheet imports each gain one segment (kwapso-design/foundations/tokens/tokens.css and kwapso-design/foundations/motion/motion.css) and every 'kwapso-design/icons' becomes 'kwapso-design/foundations/icons'. Nothing else moved by D10-B: controls/, structures/ (merged into components/ on 2026-08-26, a separate ruling), compositions/ and lib/ were all untouched by THIS move. The rows are in README.md's import table.
